questions.text: Demonstrate the use of "Encapsulation" in protecting GlobalMart’s "User Password" storage.

options.text: Allowing the "Login" screen to read the raw password from the database.
Hiding the hashing and salting logic inside a "Security" component that only returns "Match" or "No Match."
Storing the passwords in a global variable so they can be easily checked.
Encrypting the passwords with a key that is stored in the same database table.
Printing the passwords in the system logs to help with debugging.

questions.text: GlobalMart is in the "Initial Development" stage of a new "AI Chatbot." Apply the staged model to define the focus.

options.text: Fixing minor spelling errors in the chatbot's responses.
Implementing the core Natural Language Processing features and the first stable UI.
Planning the retirement of the chatbot in favor of a human support team.
Adding a "Sarcasm" feature that was requested by a single user.
Reducing the chatbot's performance to save money on cloud costs.

questions.text: Use "Regression Testing" to validate a "Database Restructuring" at GlobalMart.

options.text: Test only the new database tables and ignore the old ones.
Run the entire suite of existing functional tests to ensure that the data changes didn't break old features.
Ask the database administrator to look at the tables and see if they "look right."
Delete all old data and see if the new database can hold new data.
Only test the system on a Friday afternoon.

questions.text: Apply "Reverse Engineering" to a GlobalMart legacy module with "No Source Code" (only a .class file).

options.text: Use a de-compiler to recover the high-level Java code for analysis and modification.
Delete the .class file and ask a developer to write a new one from memory.
Try to read the binary zeros and ones to understand the module's logic.
Use a hammer to break the hard drive and see if the source code is inside.
Guess what the module does based on its file name.

questions.text: Show how "Modularity" helps GlobalMart manage "Team Collaboration."

options.text: Every developer works on the same file at the same time.
Different teams can work on the "Payment," "Inventory," and "Search" modules independently.
The team leads are the only ones allowed to write any code.
All teams must use the same programming language and the same computer.
Teams are not allowed to talk to each other to avoid "Module Contamination."

questions.text: Implement "Configuration Item" (CI) tracking for GlobalMart’s "Requirement Document."

options.text: Treat the document as a CI and put it under version control in the SCM system.
Keep the document on the project manager's personal laptop and email it when needed.
Print the document and put it in a physical filing cabinet.
Change the document whenever anyone has a new idea without telling the team.
Delete the document after the code is written to save space.

questions.text: Use the "Law of Continuing Quality" to explain why GlobalMart's system performance drops after 5 years of maintenance.

options.text: Because the hardware is getting older and slower.
Because the system's internal structure has declined due to "Entropy" and needs refactoring.
Because the users are entering more data than they used to.
Because the software is "Tired" of running for so long.
Because the company stopped paying for the "High Quality" license.

questions.text: Apply "Component-Based Design" to solve the problem of "High Development Cost" at GlobalMart.

options.text: Hire more developers to write code faster.
Use a library of pre-built, tested UI and data components instead of building everything from scratch.
Reduce the developers' salaries to lower the total cost.
Stop testing the software to save time and money.
Build the software in a country where the electricity is cheaper.

questions.text: Demonstrate how "Information Hiding" protects GlobalMart’s "Business Rules" for calculating discounts.

options.text: By putting the rules in a PDF file and sending it to all employees.
By encapsulating the discount logic in a private class that only exposes a "CalculateTotal" method.
By writing the rules in a secret language that only the CEO understands.
By making the rules a part of the user's "Terms and Conditions" on the website.
By deleting the rules after they have been programmed into the system.

questions.text: GlobalMart's system has "Data Quality Issues." Apply a re-engineering technique to handle "Redundant Data."

options.text: Keep the redundant data as a backup in case the primary data is lost.
Use "Data Normalization" to restructure the database and eliminate duplicate information.
Increase the database size so that the redundant data doesn't matter.
Delete the database and start a new one with no data at all.
Tell the users to stop entering the same information twice.

questions.text: Show how "SCM" would be used if GlobalMart's website is "Hacked" and the homepage is changed.

options.text: Use SCM to identify the unauthorized change and roll back to the last authorized baseline.
Change the homepage back manually and hope the hacker doesn't notice.
Delete the entire website and build a new one from scratch.
Close the company and move to a different country.
Ask the hacker how they changed the homepage and hire them as a consultant.

questions.text: Apply the "ISO/IEC 14764" "Problem and Modification Analysis" step to a user report that "The cart is slow."

options.text: Tell the user that the cart is not slow and they should buy a faster computer.
Analyze the performance, identify the bottleneck (e.g., a slow database query), and plan a fix.
Add a "Loading" animation to the cart to make it look faster.
Delete the cart and ask users to buy products one at a time.
Ignore the report until 100 more users complain about the same thing.

questions.text: Implement "Well-Defined Interfaces" for GlobalMart’s "Payment Gateway" to ensure "Interoperability."

options.text: Create a specific interface for every different credit card company.
Create a single, standard "IPayment" interface that any gateway (PayPal, Stripe) must implement.
Hard-code the connection to PayPal directly into the "BuyNow" button.
Ask the users to choose which payment gateway they want to use by typing its URL.
Use a different programming language for each payment gateway.

questions.text: Use "Traceability" to ensure that GlobalMart’s "New Tax Law" requirement was actually implemented.

options.text: Check the code to see if there is a comment that says "Tax Law Fixed."
Use a traceability matrix to link the legal requirement to the specific code modules and test cases.
Ask the developer if they remember fixing the tax law last Tuesday.
See if the company's total tax bill has gone down.
Check the system's "About" screen to see if it mentions the tax law.

questions.text: Apply the "Staged Model" to justify why GlobalMart's "Phase-out" system should not receive a "Security Upgrade."

options.text: Because the system is no longer used by anyone.
Because the cost and risk of the upgrade are too high for a system that will be retired soon.
Because the security upgrade would make the system too fast.
Because the company doesn't care about security during the phase-out stage.
Because the phase-out stage is managed by a different company.

questions.text: Demonstrate how "Encapsulation" helps GlobalMart's "Inventory" team update their database from "Oracle" to "PostgreSQL."

options.text: By allowing the team to change the SQL queries inside the "DataLayer" without changing the UI code.
By requiring the UI team to learn how to write PostgreSQL queries.
By making the "Oracle" database look like a "PostgreSQL" database.
By encrypting the database so that no one knows which brand it is.
By moving the database to a PostgreSQL server and hoping the Oracle code still works.

questions.text: GlobalMart’s "Legacy System" has "Architecture Degradation." Apply a "Restructuring" strategy.

options.text: Add more code to the existing system to fix the degradation.
Reorganize the internal code structure to match a modern "Layered" or "Microservices" architecture.
Buy a bigger server to hide the architecture problems.
Change the names of the files to make the architecture look more modern.
Delete the architecture and write the code in a single 1-million-line file.

questions.text: Show how "SCM Versioning" would help GlobalMart manage a "Multi-country" release (e.g., US vs UK versions).

options.text: Create two different companies to manage the two different versions.
Use SCM branching or configuration flags to maintain localized versions from a single codebase.
Copy the entire project and translate the words in the UK version.
Only release the US version and tell the UK users to use a VPN.
Change the code for the US version, then change it back for the UK version every day.

questions.text: Apply the "Law of Increasing Complexity" to explain why GlobalMart's re-engineering project is "Behind Schedule."

options.text: Because the developers are lazy and don't want to work.
Because as the system evolved, the internal dependencies became so complex that every change takes longer.
Because the project manager is using a very complex calendar.
Because the software is trying to protect itself from being re-engineered.
Because the company is using a very complex programming language.

questions.text: Implement "Perfective Maintenance" on GlobalMart’s "Search Algorithm" to improve user satisfaction.

options.text: Fix a bug that was preventing the search from showing any results.
Update the algorithm to show the most relevant products first, improving the user experience.
Change the color of the search button to "GlobalMart Blue."
Move the search bar to the bottom of the page.
Delete the search history of all users to save database space.

questions.text: Use "Static Analysis" to detect "Dead Code" in a GlobalMart legacy module.

options.text: Run the module and see which parts of the code are never executed.
Use a tool to analyze the source code and find functions that are never called by any other part of the system.
Ask the original developer which parts of the code they didn't finish.
Delete half of the code and see if the system still runs.
Look for code that is written in an old, "dead" programming language.

questions.text: Apply "Component Interoperability" to GlobalMart's "Printer Module" which needs to work with 50 different printers.

options.text: Write a different version of the module for every printer brand.
Use a "Standard Printer Interface" (like a driver model) that all printer components must follow.
Only support one brand of printer and tell the stores to buy that brand.
Ask the printer companies to change their hardware to match GlobalMart's software.
Use a physical cable to connect every printer to the main server.

questions.text: Show how "Impact Analysis" would be used when GlobalMart decides to delete the "Fax Number" field from the database.

options.text: Delete it and see who complains about their fax machine not working.
Identify all reports, UI forms, and external APIs that use the "FaxNumber" field before deleting it.
Only check the "Customer" table and ignore the "Order" table.
Ask the CEO if they still use a fax machine.
Change the name of the field to "OldFaxNumber" and leave it in the database.

questions.text: Implement "Configuration Control" for GlobalMart's "Third-Party Libraries."

options.text: Allow developers to download and use any library they find on the internet.
Maintain an approved list of libraries and versions in the SCM system to ensure security and compatibility.
Delete all third-party libraries and write everything from scratch.
Use the oldest version of every library to ensure that it is "Stable."
Hide the third-party libraries in a folder that no one can find.

questions.text: Use the "Servicing Stage" to justify why GlobalMart is "Not Adding" a social media feed to its 15-year-old payroll system.

options.text: Because social media is not allowed at work.
Because the system is in the servicing stage, where the focus is on stability and critical fixes, not new features.
Because the payroll system is not connected to the internet.
Because the employees don't want to see their social media feed while they are looking at their paychecks.
Because the company wants to build a new social media app instead.

questions.text: Apply the "Encapsulation" property to GlobalMart’s "Inventory Update" process.

options.text: Allow the "Sales" module to directly change the "QuantityOnHand" variable in the inventory database.
Require the "Sales" module to call an "UpdateInventory" method that checks for validity and security.
Send a paper memo to the inventory department every time a sale is made.
Use a global variable called "GlobalInventoryCount" that every module can access.
Encapsulate the inventory data in a password-protected zip file.

questions.text: Demonstrate how "SCM Baselines" protect GlobalMart during a "Failed Migration" to a new cloud provider.

options.text: By allowing the team to quickly revert the configuration and code to the last known stable baseline on the old server.
By providing a list of people to blame for the failed migration.
By showing the company how much money they lost during the downtime.
By creating a new baseline that includes all the errors from the failed migration.
By making the old server work faster to compensate for the failure.

questions.text: GlobalMart’s system has "Requirement Ambiguity." Apply a change-management strategy to solve this.

options.text: Ask the developers to guess what the users want and start coding.
Use a "Formal Change Request" process that requires clear documentation and stakeholder approval of requirements.
Ignore the ambiguity and wait for the users to complain after the system is released.
Change the requirements every day until everyone is happy.
Delete the requirements and use the "Agile" method of having no plan at all.

questions.text: Show how "Version Tracking" would help GlobalMart "Audit" who approved a change to the "CEO's Salary" in the payroll system.

options.text: By looking at the signature on a paper document in the CEO's office.
By reviewing the SCM metadata and pull request history to see the author and the approver of the change.
By asking the payroll manager who they think might have changed the salary.
By checking the CEO's bank account to see when the salary increased.
By running a search for the word "Salary" in the source code.

questions.text: Apply the "Reusability" principle to GlobalMart's "Error Logging" module.

options.text: Write a new error logger for every module in the system to ensure they are customized.
Create a "Global Logger Component" that provides a standard way for all modules to record errors.
Ignore all errors to save time and make the system look perfect.
Send every error as an email to the lead developer's personal phone.
Print all errors on a physical printer in the IT department.

questions.text: Implement "Software Configuration Management" (SCM) for GlobalMart’s "User Manuals."

options.text: Keep the manuals in a Google Doc that anyone with the link can edit.
Put the manuals in the SCM system along with the source code so they are versioned together.
Only write the manuals after the software is finished and never change them.
Ask the users to write their own manuals on a wiki page.
Delete the manuals and use "Tooltips" in the software instead.

questions.text: Use "Dynamic Analysis" to verify the "Performance" of GlobalMart's new "Checkout" module under heavy load.

options.text: Read the checkout code to see if there are any slow loops.
Run "Load Testing" tools to simulate 10,000 concurrent users and monitor response times and server health.
Ask 10,000 employees to log in at the same time and see what happens.
Assume the module is fast because it was written in a modern programming language.
Wait until Black Friday to see if the system crashes.

questions.text: Apply "Loose Coupling" to GlobalMart's "Currency Conversion" feature.

options.text: Hard-code the exchange rates directly into the pricing logic.
Use an external "Currency API" through a standard interface, allowing the API provider to be changed easily.
Only support US Dollars to avoid the need for currency conversion.
Store the exchange rates in a global variable that is updated manually once a year.
Ask the bank to send a fax with the exchange rates every morning.

questions.text: Demonstrate the use of "Corrective Maintenance" on GlobalMart’s "Barcode Scanner" which stops working after 100 scans.

options.text: Buy a new barcode scanner for every store.
Identify the "Memory Leak" or "Buffer Overflow" in the scanner's driver code and fix it.
Tell the employees to restart the scanner after every 99 scans.
Add a new feature that allows the scanner to read QR codes as well.
Move the barcode scanner to a different USB port on the computer.

questions.text: GlobalMart's "Legacy System" is "Not Scalable." Use re-engineering techniques to solve this.

options.text: Buy the biggest server in the world and move the system to it.
Refactor the monolithic bottleneck into "Load-Balanced" components or microservices.
Tell the users that they are not allowed to use the system at the same time.
Reduce the number of products in the inventory to make the system faster.
Change the system's name to "SuperScalableMart" to improve its reputation.

questions.text: Apply "SCM Branching" for GlobalMart's "Holiday Sale" promotion.

options.text: Modify the production code with the sale prices one week before the sale.
Create a "Holiday-Sale" branch to develop and test the promotion features independently of the main code.
Ask all developers to stop working on other features until the holiday sale is over.
Use a different website for the holiday sale and link to it from the main page.
Write the holiday sale code in a different programming language.

questions.text: Show how "Impact Analysis" helps GlobalMart manage "Risk" during a major UI redesign.

options.text: It tells the team how much the users will hate the new design.
It identifies which backend APIs and data structures will need to change to support the new UI.
It calculates the physical impact of the new UI on the user's eyes.
It ensures that the new UI is compatible with every mobile phone in the world.
It allows the team to skip the testing phase if the impact is "Low."

questions.text: Implement "Version Tracking" for GlobalMart’s "Database Schema" changes.

options.text: Use "Migration Scripts" (like Flyway or Liquibase) that are stored in the SCM system to track and apply changes.
Ask the database administrator to keep a list of changes in a notebook.
Change the database schema manually and don't tell anyone.
Use a "Schema Comparison" tool to find out what changed after the system crashes.
Delete the old database schema every time a new one is created.

questions.text: Use the "Law of Continuing Change" to explain why GlobalMart's 30-year-old mainframe system is "Still Being Updated."

options.text: Because the company has a contract with the mainframe manufacturer.
Because if the system stops evolving to match the business's current needs, it will become useless.
Because the mainframe is so powerful that it can never be replaced.
Because the developers who built the mainframe are still working there.
Because the government requires all mainframes to be updated once a year.

questions.text: Apply "Perfective Maintenance" to GlobalMart's "Mobile App" login screen.

options.text: Fix a bug that was preventing users from logging in with a capital letter in their email.
Implement "Biometric Login" (FaceID/Fingerprint) to make the login process faster and more secure for users.
Update the app to work on the latest version of iOS.
Change the "Login" button text to "Sign In."
Delete the login screen and let everyone access the app for free.

questions.text: Demonstrate how "Encapsulation" helps GlobalMart's "Tax Module" handle "International Sales."

options.text: By exposing the specific tax laws of every country to the "Checkout" module.
By hiding the complex international tax logic and only providing a "CalculateTax(CountryCode, Amount)" method.
By requiring the customer to calculate their own tax based on their country.
By using a different tax module for every different country.
By only selling products in countries that have the same tax laws as the US.

questions.text: GlobalMart’s "Component-Based System" has a "Security Vulnerability" in the "Login Component." Implement a fix.

options.text: Rewrite the entire system from scratch to ensure it is secure.
Replace the "Login Component" with a newer, secure version without changing the rest of the system.
Tell the users to change their passwords every hour.
Disable the login feature until a fix is found.
Hide the vulnerability by changing the name of the "Login" folder.

questions.text: Show how "SCM baselines" would be used if GlobalMart's "Version 3.0" is found to be "Slower" than "Version 2.0."

options.text: Compare the performance metrics of Version 3.0 against the Version 2.0 baseline to identify where the slowdown occurred.
Delete Version 3.0 and tell the users to go back to using Version 2.0.
Fire the developers who worked on Version 3.0.
Add more hardware to the Version 3.0 server until it is faster than Version 2.0.
Change the version number of 3.0 back to 2.0 so the users don't notice.

questions.text: Apply "Adaptive Maintenance" to GlobalMart’s "Payment System" when "Apple Pay" becomes a popular payment method.

options.text: Fix a bug in the "Credit Card" processing logic.
Modify the system to integrate Apple Pay as a new payment option for customers.
Improve the speed of the "PayPal" integration.
Delete the "Cash on Delivery" option because no one uses it anymore.
Change the "Payment" page's background color to match Apple's brand.

questions.text: Implement "Configuration Item" tracking for GlobalMart’s "Test Data."

options.text: Treat the test data as a CI and store it in the SCM system to ensure tests are repeatable.
Use random data every time a test is run to keep the system "On its toes."
Ask the developers to use their own personal data for testing.
Delete the test data after the tests are finished to save disk space.
Use a physical printout of the test data and enter it manually for every test.

questions.text: Use "Impact Analysis" to justify why GlobalMart's "Change Request #402" was "Rejected."

options.text: Because the project manager didn't like the person who submitted the request.
Because the analysis showed that the change would break 10 critical modules and cost $50,000 to fix.
Because the change request was written in a font that was too small to read.
Because the change request was submitted on a Friday afternoon.
Because the system is already "Perfect" and doesn't need any changes.

questions.text: Apply the "Phase-out" stage guidelines to GlobalMart's "Windows XP" based store kiosks.

options.text: Upgrade the kiosks to Windows 11 immediately.
Plan the migration of the kiosk software to a modern web-based platform and stop adding features to the XP version.
Paint the kiosks a new color to make them look more modern.
Hire 10 new Windows XP experts to maintain the kiosks for the next 20 years.
Turn off the kiosks and tell the customers to use their phones instead.

questions.text: Demonstrate how "Traceability" helps GlobalMart's "QA Team" verify that all "Bug Fixes" were tested.

options.text: By asking the developers which bugs they fixed today.
By using a "Traceability Matrix" to link every bug report to a specific fix in the code and a corresponding test case.
By checking the system's "Error Log" and seeing if it is empty.
By running the system and waiting for it to crash.
By counting the number of lines of code that were changed during the bug fix.

questions.text: GlobalMart's "Data Reverse Engineering" project is "Recovering Business Rules." Implement a strategy for this.

options.text: Ask the oldest employee in the company how the system works.
Analyze the stored procedures, triggers, and data constraints in the legacy database to extract the logic.
Read the "User Manual" from 1995 to find the business rules.
Guess the business rules based on the names of the database tables.
Delete the database and write new business rules from scratch.

questions.text: Apply "SCM Release Management" to GlobalMart's "2024 Black Friday" update.

options.text: Release the update to all stores at the same time on Black Friday morning.
Use a "Staged Release" or "Canary Deployment" to test the update in a few stores before a full rollout.
Wait until the Monday after Black Friday to release the update.
Only release the update to stores that are having a big sale.
Ask the store managers to install the update themselves using a USB drive.
